evidence.title: Binance on-chain delegated authority persisted beyond operational shutdown
evidence.observation: Binance reports that suspending withdrawals and shutting down hot-wallet services did not automatically invalidate existing EIP-7702 on-chain authorizations. Separate revocation transactions were required.
evidence.evidence_standing: Source-reported bounded observation; not independently verified
evidence.glossary_fit: Commons interpretation only; founding definitions and standings unchanged

source_locations.SRC-152: What happened on 29 October, paragraphs on EIP-7702 delegation, withdrawal suspension, service shutdown and revocation; opening investigation qualification

evidence.limitations: Initial issuer account; not independently verified. Persistence of delegated execution authority does not establish continued AI activity, agent trajectory persistence or system-level autonomy. The source reports eventual revocation, not permanent loss of control.
evidence.open_questions: Which shutdown and revocation mechanisms cover delegated execution rights across the relevant authority boundaries? The Commons has not independently reconstructed the incident.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: Containment within one operational boundary did not revoke authority already delegated across another. This concerns the practical reach of corrective action; it is distinct from the AI-tool compromise in EVID-189.

terms.name: Governability
terms.definition: A property of a consequential process describing the extent to which legitimate parties can understand, influence, constrain, correct, or recover its operation and outcomes. It does not imply complete predictability or a single controller.

relationships.explanation: Commons interpretation: Binance's reported shutdown/revocation mismatch illustrates a boundary in corrective authority over a consequential process: operational shutdown did not itself revoke on-chain delegation. Separate revocation eventually succeeded. This technology-neutral finding does not establish continued AI activity or permanent uncontrollability.
